rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a change of direction after something hits the ground or an obstacle.

example.english: The ball took a bounce off the wall and came back.
example.traditional: 個波撞到牆之後有反彈，返咗嚟。
example.jyutping: go3 bo1 zong6 dou2 coeng4 zi1 hau6 jau5 faan2 taan4 faan1 zo2 lei4

rows.note: Use 彈 for ordinary up-and-down motion, including bouncing a child, and colloquially for a cheque being refused by the bank.

example.english: I gently bounce my grandson up and down.
example.traditional: 我抱住個孫仔輕輕咁彈下彈下。
example.jyutping: ngo5 pou5 zyu6 go3 syun1 zai2 hing1 hing1 gam2 taan4 haa5 taan4 haa5

rows.note: Use this for the up-and-down bouncing movement itself, especially in sports or when describing an object's movement.

example.english: Look at the basketball bounce up and down.
example.traditional: 你睇吓個籃球喺度彈跳。
example.jyutping: nei5 tai2 haa5 go3 laam4 kau4 hai2 dou6 taan4 tiu3

rows.note: Use 走 as the all-purpose casual verb when someone is leaving or going away.

example.jyutping: si4 gaan1 m4 zou2 laa3 ngo5 dei6 zau2 laa3

rows.note: Use 反彈 when something rebounds after impact, including a ball off a wall or an aircraft bouncing on landing.

example.english: The ball did bounce back after hitting the wall.
example.traditional: 個波撞到牆之後反彈返嚟。
example.jyutping: go3 bo1 zong6 dou3 coeng4 zi1 hau6 faan2 taan4 faan1 lei4

rows.note: Use this construction when you put an idea to someone for discussion or feedback rather than literally bouncing it.

example.english: I want to bounce the idea of a raise off my boss.
example.traditional: 我想同老闆傾吓加人工。
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 tung4 lou5 baan2 king1 haa5 gaa1 jan4 gung1
